title_youtube: Voyager 1 Is Now One Light-Day Away. Light Needs 24 Hours to Reach It
description_youtube:
Voyager 1 is now one light-day from Earth: a radio signal moving at the speed of light needs a full 24 hours to reach it. NASA's Voyager 1 crossed that line on Nov. 18, 2026.

The numbers:
- About 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion km) from Earth, the farthest spacecraft humans have ever flown.
- Launched in 1977, still moving at about 38,000 mph.
- 24 hours for a command to get there, 24 hours for the answer to come back. NASA sends it commands about once a week.
- Its three onboard computers hold 69.63 kilobytes of memory in total, less than a single phone photo.
- On Nov. 14, 2026 it went quiet: no science or engineering data, only its carrier signal (the "hum"). As of Nov. 19, NASA engineers were analyzing the problem.

Would you keep waiting for that reply? Tell us below.

Sources:
- NASA JPL, Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth (Nov. 19, 2026): https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/nasas-voyager-1-makes-history-reaching-one-light-day-from-earth/
